set.layering_notes: Alameda County unincorporated areas (Ashland, Cherryland, San Lorenzo, Castro Valley, Fairview, Sunol) have no local inclusionary production or fee revenue, so county-controlled affordable housing there depends on A1, Measure W and HACA. Expect an inclusionary requirement on market-rate projects entitled after mid-2027. Density bonus alone does not trigger prevailing wage. Classified as regulatory requirement because the county-specific content is a pending inclusionary ordinance (a set-aside obligation, not a subsidy); the state density bonus portion is covered by Government Code 65915 and is available now. Sources opened: County affordable housing production policies page (re-read November 8, 2026) and the Jan 26, 2026 staff report.
set.audit_note: Reclassified from density bonus to regulatory requirement. Policies page re-read November 8, 2026: ordinance not adopted; draft ordinances early 2027, recommendations spring 2027, project completion July 2027; ownership units may range up to 150% AMI.

reason: Record is primarily a pending county inclusionary ordinance, which SCHEMA.md classes as regulatory requirement; page confirms it is not yet adopted.

The source is a 2017 EveryOne Home deck that confirms only the 2017 five-year policy (20% of prior-year receipts, $5 million minimum, $7.5 million maximum), and no current County page stating a boomerang housing allocation, cycle or amount could be found.

set.typical_award_size: Linkage fee on office and warehouse projects over 25,000 sq ft: $7.87 per sq ft for permits applied July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025 per Table 4 ($8.05 for July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024), inflation adjusted; paid 25% at permit, 50% at certificate of occupancy, 25% eighteen months later. The 2025 amendments extended the fee to additional nonresidential categories. FY 2024-25 JHIF fund (Fund 1871): start $13,964,433, end $12,546,460, fee revenue $0 in FY 2024-25, $12,060,074 committed to affordable developments, $486,386 being committed to pipeline projects. Past JHIF awards include $2,500,000 (2700 International, 75 units) and $3,472,130 (34th and San Pablo, 60 units).
set.layering_notes: Oakland is one of only two priority cities in the county with a commercial linkage fee (Fremont also has one). Classified as loan because the fund balance is deployed as City development loans through HCD NOFAs (New Construction and ACAH); the fee itself is a cost to commercial developers, not to affordable housing sponsors. Revenue is modest relative to Measure U (FY 2024-25 JHIF fee revenue was $0) but is flexible local money with no bond restrictions, which HCD uses for early predevelopment commitments. Developers do not apply to this fund directly; it is part of the NOFA sources table.
set.audit_note: Reclassified from other to loan per audit rule for trust funds that deploy loans. Impact Fee Annual Report FY 2024-25 (CED Committee February 10, 2026) shows JHIF committed to projects through City loans.

reason: The FY 2024-25 Impact Fee Annual Report shows JHIF Fund 1871 is deployed as City loans to affordable developments via NOFAs, so loan is the best enum.

Chapter 18.290 (zoneomics mirror) defines affordable housing at 120% AMI but contains no 50% reduction or affordable-specific deferral, fremont.gov fee pages and published documents return 403, and no stated prevailing wage rule for the fee reduction was found (searched the code text and city fee documents).

set.typical_award_size: FY 2025/26 CDBG: entitlement $1,579,819 plus $121,143 program income and $408,685 reprogrammed funds, total $2,109,647; about $1,008,291 available for capital projects. FY 2025/26 capital awards ranged from $50,000 to $465,280 (MidPen Century Village rehabilitation $465,280). ESG entitlement $146,207. Fremont also receives a formula share of the Alameda County HOME Consortium allocation; the HOME dollar amount was not stated in the staff report.
set.cycle_notes: CDBG and ESG are allocated in two-year funding cycles with an annual capital proposal round. FY 2025/26 round: proposal workshop January 9, 2025, proposals due February 6, 2025, Citizens Advisory Committee recommendations March 27, 2025, Council adoption July 8, 2025. RFP advertised in the newspaper, City web page and cable channel.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Based on the FY 2025/26 schedule, the next CDBG capital proposal round is expected to open in winter with proposals due around February 2027; confirm with Human Services.
